description: Canonical circuit cryptographic constructions: CircuitId derivation (from commitment_root), HKDF hop key derivation (salt=commitment_root), nonce prefix derivation, nonce layout, and replay guard. All inputs use the reconciled spec/08 model.
statusNote: reference-implemented — all constructions use the reconciled spec/08 model: BLAKE3, commitment_root as input/salt, 64-bit nonce prefix + 32-bit frame_sequence.

vectors.name: hop-keys-deterministic
vectors.description: HKDF-SHA256(salt=commitment_root, ikm=sharedSecret, info=SHARENET/CIRCUIT/KEY/1 || u8(hopIndex)) → 64 bytes split 32/32

vectors.name: nonce-prefix-deterministic
vectors.description: Nonce prefix = first 8 bytes of HKDF-SHA256(salt=commitment_root, ikm=initiator_x25519_pub, info='SHARENET/CIRCUIT/NONCE/1'). Per ADR-0020: the nonce prefix is bound to the CIRCUIT INSTANCE (root + initiator ephemeral public key), so a re-key on the same route produces a fresh nonce prefix.

vectors.name: nonce-layout
vectors.description: nonce = circuit_nonce_prefix (8 bytes) || frame_sequence (4 bytes big-endian) = 12 bytes

vectors.name: nonce-prefix-re-key-freshness
vectors.description: Two circuits on the SAME route (same commitment_root) with DIFFERENT initiator ephemeral keys produce DIFFERENT nonce prefixes. Per spec/08 §4.7 + ADR-0020: a re-key MUST produce a fresh circuit_nonce_prefix. Under the old derivation (pre-980ced6, bound to root only), both would be the same — contradicting §4.7. Under the corrected derivation (bound to root + initiator eph pub), they differ.

verification: TS+Python runners independently reproduce the exact bytes from the reference implementation.
